title: Knowledge_compilation
summary:
Knowledge compilation is a family of approaches for addressing the intractability of a number of artificial intelligence problems. A propositional model is compiled in an off-line phase in order to support some queries in polynomial time, and many ways of compiling a propositional model exist.

A key contribution to this area is the knowledge compilation map, which proposes analyzing different compilation approaches according to two key dimensions: the succinctness of the target compilation language, and the class of queries and transformations that the language supports in polynomial time. The knowledge compilation map analyzes a large number of existing target compilation languages, going beyond classical flat target compilation languages based on CNF and DNF, and considering a richer nested class based on directed acyclic graphs such as OBDDs (Ordered Binary Decision Diagrams).

Knowledge compilation is closely related to knowledge representation and reasoning, a field of artificial intelligence that focuses on designing computer representations that capture information about the world that can be used for solving complex problems. One of the main purposes of explicitly representing knowledge is to be able to reason about that knowledge, to make inferences, assert new knowledge, and apply it to problem-solving tasks. The compilation approach allows expensive reasoning to be shifted to an offline preprocessing phase, enabling efficient online query answering.
